Stop Teeth Shifting

Bite Problems? Restore Balance

Missing teeth cause other teeth to shift, which can lead to bite changes, which may contribute to TMJ symptoms and chewing difficulties. Implants restore your bite.

Free 15-Min Chat1-Hour Consultation — £80Call 020 71833573

✓ Full Bite Analysis · ✓ Prevent Further Damage · ✓ 0% Finance*

Teeth are designed to support each other. When one is lost, the stability of the entire arch is compromised. It is not just about the gap; it is about what happens to the remaining teeth.

Without the support of their neighbors, adjacent teeth begin to drift or tilt into the empty space. Similarly, the opposing tooth (the one above or below the gap) may "over-erupt" or grow outwards because it has nothing to bite against.

This shifting leads to Bite Collapse, which can cause chronic jaw pain (TMJ), uneven wear on healthy teeth, and headaches. At Dental Implants London, we use implants to act as a "doorstop," helping stabilise the bite and reduce the risk of future movement.

Consequences of Untreated Gaps

Drifting & Tilting

Adjacent teeth lean into the gap, creating hard-to-clean pockets that harbor bacteria and lead to further tooth loss.

TMJ Strain

An uneven bite forces your jaw muscles to work harder to find a comfortable resting position, leading to chronic pain and clicking joints.

Uneven Wear

When teeth are missing, the remaining teeth take on extra load, causing them to wear down flat, chip, or crack prematurely.

Facial Shortening

Severe bite collapse can reduce the height of the lower face, causing the chin to protrude which may contribute to changes in facial appearance over time.

Restorative Strategy

Restoring Equilibrium

Correcting a collapsed bite often requires a comprehensive approach. We don't just fill the gap; we look at the whole system.

Implant Stabilization

Placing an implant may help prevent adjacent teeth from drifting into the gap over time.

Bite Raising

If wear is severe, we can rebuild the height of worn teeth with crowns or bonding alongside your implants.

Orthodontics (Optional)

In severe drift cases, we may use aligners to upright the tilted teeth before placing the implant.
